title: AI Surrogate Model for Distributed Computing Workloads
problem: Large-scale scientific experiments require optimized data placement and payload allocation in distributed computing systems. Current decision-making processes are heuristic and disjointed, while machine learning approaches lack sufficient training data and raise privacy concerns.
motivation: ML-based optimization of resource allocation in distributed scientific computing can improve efficiency, but requires extensive real-world data while preserving privacy.
method: The authors train four generative models (TVAE, CTAGGAN+, SMOTE, TabDDPM) on 2+ million real job submission records from 150 days of operations. They evaluate synthetic data fidelity using feature-wise distribution analysis, pair-wise feature correlations, distance to closest records, and pre-trained model responses. A probabilistic diffusion-based model (TabDDPM) is selected as optimal for balancing data quality with privacy.
key_novelty: Using generative surrogate modeling to synthesize realistic job submission records while preserving privacy, enabling ML-based workload optimization without requiring extensive real data access.
contributions: Collected and processed 2+ million real job submission records over 150 days from large-scale scientific collaborations
Comprehensive evaluation of four generative models (TVAE, CTAGGAN+, SMOTE, TabDDPM) for tabular workload data
Demonstrated TabDDPM as optimal for synthetic data fidelity and privacy preservation compared to SMOTE and other generative approaches
Validated synthetic job records as training data for ML-based resource optimization systems

metrics.other: data fidelity (distribution similarity, feature correlations), privacy preservation

primary_theme: Generative modeling for synthetic HPC workload generation
